entities.name: Black Riders
entities.summary: Spearmen on black horses in black armour, with bowmen, led by the elder brother of the drowned nephew.

refs.q: well mounted on black horses and clad in black armour

entities.name: (unnamed) brother of the Utterbol nephew
entities.summary: Brother of the drowned nephew, nearly as old as Gandolf; a good warrior, wise leader and skilled raider.

refs.q: the men of the brother of thy hot wooer, Lady Ursula, whom I cooled in the Ram's Bane, but a man well nigh as old as his uncle

entities.name: Michael-a-green
entities.summary: Utterbol man who unfurls the Bull pennon.

refs.q: thou, Michael-a-green shake out the Bull

entities.name: (unnamed) field of the betrayal
entities.summary: Plain by a wood where Ralph was taken by the Lord of Utterbol, with a rowan tree.

refs.q: Lo, beloved, this quicken-tree; hereby it was that the tent was pitched wherein I lay the night when I was taken
these are the men of the brother of thy hot wooer
the Black men-at-arms came on at a trot
They slept in no house that night nor for many nights after; for they were now fairly on the waste

facts.subject: Black Riders
facts.statement: Black armour and black horses; bowmen from a thicket; a screeching yell as they charge.

refs.q: with a great screeching yell cast their spears into the rest

facts.subject: Bull Shockhead
facts.statement: Utterbol's men take no prisoners from raiders; sixteen enemies slain, four of theirs.

refs.q: The Utterbol Riders had slain sixteen of their foemen; for they took none to mercy

facts.subject: Bull Shockhead
facts.statement: Fowlers and peat-cutters in the waste bow to Utterbol's token.

refs.q: naught save a fowler of the waste, or a peat-cutter, who stood to look on the men-at-arms going by, and made obeisance to the token of Utterbol

facts.subject: Ursula
facts.statement: Ursula wears a hauberk and steel coif in battle; a javelin fails to pierce it.

refs.q: steel kept out steel: I have no scratch or point or edge on me

facts.subject: Redhead
facts.statement: Redhead says the true test of a man is fighting fresh foes one after another until longing for night or death.

refs.q: That which trieth a man, is to fight and overcome, and straight have to fight with fresh foemen

events.label: Battle with the Black Riders
places: (unnamed) waste between Vale Turris and Goldburg
events.summary: On the fifth day the Utterbol escort routs the Black Riders; Ursula is struck but unhurt.

refs.q: in five minutes' time the Black Riders were fleeing all over the field
a man well nigh as old as his uncle, though he hath not made men tremble so sore

opportunities.idea: Rival heirs of a deposed tyrant as ongoing border raiders, a source of escort encounters.

basis_refs.q: 'tis not unlike that we shall have to speak to his men again, either out-going or home-coming

ledger.summary: They cross the waste with a light tent for Ursula, meeting only fowlers and peat-cutters who bow to Utterbol's token. On the fifth day spears appear by a thicket: the Black Riders, on black horses in black armour, the men of the slain nephew's brother, a reiver nearly as old as his uncle but a better man. Redhead has the Bull pennon shaken out by Michael-a-green and the horn blown. The bands clash; Ralph spears a tall man and fights with the Upmeads blade; the Black Riders flee, with sixteen slain to Utterbol's four. A javelin strikes Ursula, but her hauberk holds. Later they reach the field where Ralph was betrayed and camp by the same rowan tree.
ledger.geography_notes: The road west from Vale Turris crosses waste: no houses, fowlers and peat-cutters. A thicket on the fifth day. Later, the plain by a wood where the Lord of Utterbol once camped and Ralph was taken, with a rowan (quicken) tree marking the tent site.
